questions.stem: What do we learn about the woman's store?

options.A: It focuses exclusively on jazz.
options.B: It sponsors major jazz concerts.
options.C: It has several branches in London.
options.D: It displays albums by new music talents.

questions.cn: 关于女士的店，我们了解到什么？

optionsCn.B: 它赞助主要爵士音乐会。
optionsCn.D: 它展示新音乐人才的专辑。

questions.stem: What does the man say about jazz music?

options.A: It originated with cowboys.
options.B: Its market has now shrunk.
options.C: Its listeners are mostly young people.
options.D: It remains as widespread as hip hop music.

questions.cn: 关于爵士乐，男士说了什么？

optionsCn.C: 它的听众大多是年轻人。
optionsCn.D: 它仍和嘻哈音乐一样流行。

questions.stem: What does the woman say about jazz?

options.A: Its definition is varied and complicated.
options.B: It is still going through experimentation.
options.C: It is frequently accompanied by singing.
options.D: Its style has remained largely unchanged.

questions.cn: 关于爵士乐，女士说了什么？

optionsCn.D: 它的风格基本保持不变。

questions.stem: What should you do to appreciate different styles of jazz according to the woman?

options.A: Learn to play them.
options.B: Take music lessons.
options.C: Listen to them yourself.
options.D: Consult jazz musicians.

questions.cn: 根据女士，要欣赏不同风格的爵士乐，你应该做什么？

optionsCn.D: 咨询爵士音乐家。

lines.t: Conversation 1.
lines.cn: 对话一。

lines.t: M: Excuse me, where's your rock music section?
lines.cn: M：打扰一下，你们的摇滚乐区在哪？

lines.t: F: Rock music? I'm sorry, we're a jazz store. We don't have any rock and roll.
lines.cn: F：摇滚乐？抱歉，我们是家爵士乐唱片店。我们没有任何摇滚乐。

lines.t: M: Oh, you only have jazz music? Nothing else?
lines.cn: M：哦，你们只有爵士乐？没有别的？

lines.t: F: That's right. We're the only record store in London dedicated exclusively to jazz.
lines.cn: F：没错。我们是伦敦唯一一家只专营爵士乐的唱片店。

lines.t: F: Actually, we're more than just a record store. We have a cafe and library upstairs,
lines.cn: F：其实，我们不只是一家唱片店。楼上有咖啡厅和图书馆，

lines.t: F: and a ticket office down the hall where you can buy tickets to all the major jazz concerts in the city.
lines.cn: F：走廊尽头还有售票处，可以买到本市所有主要爵士音乐会的门票。

lines.t: F: Also, we have our own studio next door where we produce albums for up-and-coming artists.
lines.cn: F：此外，隔壁还有我们自己的录音棚，为崭露头角的艺术家制作专辑。

lines.t: F: We're committed to fostering new music talent.
lines.cn: F：我们致力于培养新的音乐人才。

lines.t: M: Wow, that's so cool. I guess there's not much of a jazz scene anymore, not like there used to be.
lines.cn: M：哇，太酷了。我想爵士乐的圈子已经不像从前那样了。

lines.t: M: But here you're trying to promote this great music genre.
lines.cn: M：但你们正在努力推广这种伟大的音乐类型。

lines.t: F: Yes, indeed. Nowadays, most people like to listen to pop and rock music.
lines.cn: F：是的，的确如此。如今，大多数人喜欢听流行音乐和摇滚乐。

lines.t: F: Hip-hop music from America is also getting more and more popular.
lines.cn: F：来自美国的嘻哈音乐也越来越受欢迎。

lines.t: F: So as a result, there are fewer listeners of jazz, which is a great shame, because it's an incredibly rich genre.
lines.cn: F：结果是，爵士乐的听众变少了，这非常可惜，因为它是一种极其丰富的音乐类型。

lines.t: F: But that's not to say there isn't any good new jazz music being made out there anymore. Far from it.
lines.cn: F：但这并不是说外面就不再有好听的新爵士乐了。远非如此。

lines.t: F: It's just a much smaller market today.
lines.cn: F：只是如今的市场小得多。

lines.t: M: So how would you define jazz?
lines.cn: M：那你会怎么定义爵士乐？

lines.t: F: Well, interestingly enough, there's no agreed-upon definition of jazz.
lines.cn: F：嗯，有意思的是，爵士乐并没有一个公认的统一定义。

lines.t: F: Indeed, there are many different styles of jazz. Some have singing, but most don't.
lines.cn: F：的确，爵士乐有许多不同的风格。有些带演唱，但大多数没有。

lines.t: F: Some are electric and some aren't. Some contain live experimentation, but not always.
lines.cn: F：有些用电声，有些不用。有些包含现场即兴实验，但也不一定。

lines.t: F: While there's no simple definition for it, and while there are many different styles of jazz, you simply know it when you hear it.
lines.cn: F：虽然它没有简单的定义、虽然爵士乐有许多不同风格，但你一听就能认出它。

lines.t: F: Honestly, the only way to know what jazz is, is listen to it yourself.
lines.cn: F：说实话，想知道爵士乐是什么，唯一的办法就是亲自去听。

lines.t: F: As the great trumpet player Louis Armstrong said,
lines.cn: F：正如伟大的小号手路易斯·阿姆斯特朗所说，

lines.t: F: If you gotta ask, you'll never know.
lines.cn: F：如果你还要问，你就永远不会懂。

questions.stem: What did the woman do this morning?

options.A: She paid her mortgage.
options.B: She called on the man.
options.C: She made a business plan.
options.D: She went to the bank.

questions.cn: 今天上午女士做了什么？

optionsCn.D: 她去了银行。

questions.stem: Why was the woman's proposal rejected?

options.A: Her previous debt hadn't been cleared yet.
options.B: Her credit history was considered poor.
options.C: She had apparently asked for too much.
options.D: She didn't pay her mortgage in time.

questions.cn: 女士的申请为什么被拒？

optionsCn.A: 她之前的债务尚未还清。
optionsCn.B: 她的信用记录被认为不佳。
optionsCn.D: 她没有按时还房贷。

questions.stem: What is the woman planning to do?

options.A: Pay a debt long overdue.
options.B: Buy a piece of property.
options.C: Start her own business.
options.D: Check her credit history.

questions.cn: 女士计划做什么？

optionsCn.A: 偿还一笔拖欠已久的债务。
optionsCn.D: 核查她的信用记录。

questions.stem: What does the man suggest the woman do?

options.A: Seek advice from an expert about fundraising.
options.B: Ask for smaller loans from different lenders.
options.C: Build up her own finances step by step.
options.D: Revise her business proposal carefully.

questions.cn: 男士建议女士怎么做？

optionsCn.B: 向不同的放贷方申请小额贷款。
optionsCn.C: 一步步积累自己的财务实力。
optionsCn.D: 仔细修改她的商业申请。

lines.t: Conversation 2.
lines.cn: 对话二。

lines.t: M: How did it go at the bank this morning?
lines.cn: M：今天上午去银行怎么样？

lines.t: F: Not well. My proposal was rejected.
lines.cn: F：不顺利。我的申请被拒了。

lines.t: M: Really? But why?
lines.cn: M：真的吗？为什么？

lines.t: F: Bunch of reasons. For starters, they said my credit history was not good enough.
lines.cn: F：一堆理由。首先，他们说我的信用记录不够好。

lines.t: M: Did they say how you could improve that?
lines.cn: M：他们说怎么改善了吗？

lines.t: F: Yes. They said that after five more years of paying my mortgage,
lines.cn: F：说了。他们说再还五年房贷之后，

lines.t: F: then I would become a more viable candidate for a business loan.
lines.cn: F：我才能成为商业贷款更合格的候选人。

lines.t: F: But right now, it's too risky for them to lend me money.
lines.cn: F：但现在，借钱给我对他们来说风险太大。

lines.t: F: They fear I will default on any business loan I'm given.
lines.cn: F：他们担心我拿到任何商业贷款都会违约。

lines.t: M: Well, that doesn't sound fair. Your business idea is amazing.
lines.cn: M：嗯，这听起来不公平。你的商业点子很棒。

lines.t: M: Did you show them your business plan? What did they say?
lines.cn: M：你给他们看你的商业计划了吗？他们怎么说？

lines.t: F: They didn't really articulate any position regarding the actual business plan.
lines.cn: F：他们对商业计划本身其实没有明确表态。

lines.t: F: They simply looked at my credit history and determined it was not good enough.
lines.cn: F：他们只是看了我的信用记录，就认定它不够好。

lines.t: F: They said the bank has strict guidelines and requirements as to who they can lend money to.
lines.cn: F：他们说，银行对能把钱借给谁有严格的准则和要求。

lines.t: F: And I simply don't meet their financial threshold.
lines.cn: F：而我就是达不到他们的财务门槛。

lines.t: M: Why haven't you asked for a smaller amount? Maybe you could gather capital from other sources.
lines.cn: M：你为什么不申请一笔小一点的数额？也许你可以从其他渠道筹钱。

lines.t: F: Smaller loans from more lenders?
lines.cn: F：向更多放贷方申请小额贷款？

lines.t: F: You don't get it. It doesn't matter the size of the loan I ask for
lines.cn: F：你没明白。我要申请的贷款金额大小并不重要，

lines.t: F: or the type of business I propose. That's all inconsequential.
lines.cn: F：我提出的是什么类型的生意也不重要。这些都无关紧要。

lines.t: F: The first thing every bank will do is study how much money I have and how much debt I have
lines.cn: F：每家银行要做的第一件事，就是研究我有多少钱、欠多少债，

lines.t: F: before they decide whether or not to lend me any more money.
lines.cn: F：然后才决定要不要再借给我钱。

lines.t: F: If I want to continue ahead with this dream of owning my own business,
lines.cn: F：如果我想继续推进这个拥有自己事业的梦想，

lines.t: F: I have no other choice but to build up my own finances.
lines.cn: F：我没有别的选择，只能积累起自己的财务实力。

lines.t: F: I need around 20% more in personal savings and 50% less debt. That's all there is to it.
lines.cn: F：我需要个人储蓄再多 20% 左右、债务减少 50%。就是这么回事。

lines.t: M: I see now. Well, it's a huge pity that they rejected your request, but don't lose hope.
lines.cn: M：我现在明白了。嗯，他们拒绝了你的请求真是太遗憾了，但别失去希望。

lines.t: M: I still think that your idea is great and that you would turn it into a phenomenal success.
lines.cn: M：我仍然认为你的点子很棒，你会把它做成巨大的成功。

questions.stem: What do we learn about Leo Sanchez's farm?

options.A: It is profitable and environmentally friendly.
options.B: It is well located and completely automated.
options.C: It is small and unconventional.
options.D: It is fertile and productive.

questions.cn: 关于利奥·桑切斯的农场，我们了解到什么？

optionsCn.B: 它位置好且完全自动化。
optionsCn.D: 它肥沃而高产。

questions.stem: What has motivated Leo Sanchez and his fellow young farmers to engage in farming?

options.A: Their urge to make farming more enjoyable.
options.B: Their desire to improve farming equipment.
options.C: Their hope to revitalize traditional farming.
options.D: Their wish to set a new farming standard.

questions.cn: 是什么激励利奥·桑切斯和年轻农夫同伴投身农业？

optionsCn.A: 他们想让务农更有乐趣。
optionsCn.C: 他们希望振兴传统农业。
optionsCn.D: 他们希望为农业设立新标准。

questions.stem: Why did Leo Sanchez buy a hand-operated weeding tool?

options.A: It saves a lot of electricity.
options.B: It needs little maintenance.
options.C: It causes hardly any pollution.
options.D: It loosens soil while weeding.

questions.cn: 利奥·桑切斯为什么买了一件手动除草工具？

optionsCn.D: 它除草时还能松土。

lines.t: Passage 1.
lines.cn: 短文一。

lines.t: There's a lot about Leo Sanchez and his farm in Salinas, California that seems unusual.
lines.cn: 关于利奥·桑切斯和他的加利福尼亚州萨利纳斯农场，有许多看似不寻常之处。

lines.t: The national average farm size is around 440 acres, but his is only one acre.
lines.cn: 全国农场平均规模约 440 英亩，但他的只有一英亩。

lines.t: The average age of farmers hovers around 58 years old, but he is just 26.
lines.cn: 农场主的平均年龄在 58 岁上下，但他只有 26 岁。

lines.t: And Sanchez constantly attempts to improve everything from seeding techniques out in the field to the promotion and sale of his produce online.
lines.cn: 而且桑切斯不断尝试改进一切，从田间的播种技术，到农产品的线上推广与销售。

lines.t: This is evidence of an experimental approach.
lines.cn: 这是一种实验性做法的证据。

lines.t: It's an approach not dictated by the confines of conventional, large-scale agriculture led by international corporations.
lines.cn: 这种做法不受由跨国公司主导的传统大规模农业的条条框框约束。

lines.t: While farming is often difficult for both the body and mind, Sanchez says he and many of his fellow young farmers are motivated by a desire to set a new standard for agriculture.
lines.cn: 虽然务农对身心都是件苦差事，但桑切斯说，他和许多年轻农夫同伴的动力，是希望为农业设立一个新标准。

lines.t: Many of them are employing a multitude of technologies, some new and some not so new.
lines.cn: 他们中的许多人在使用多种技术，有些是新的，有些没那么新。

lines.t: Recently, Sanchez bought a hand-operated tool which pulls out weeds and loosens soil.
lines.cn: 最近，桑切斯买了一件手动的除草松土工具。

lines.t: It actually dates back to at least 1701.
lines.cn: 它其实至少可以追溯到 1701 年。

lines.t: It stands in sharp contrast to Sanchez's other gadget, a gas-powered flame weed killer invented in 1997.
lines.cn: 这与他的另一件设备形成鲜明对比——一件 1997 年发明的燃气火焰除草器。

lines.t: He simply doesn't discriminate when it comes to the newness of tools. If it works, it works.
lines.cn: 对于工具的新旧，他毫不挑拣。好用就行。

lines.t: Farmers have a long history of invention and it's no different today.
lines.cn: 农夫有着悠久的发明史，如今也不例外。

lines.t: Young farmers are guided by their love for agriculture and aided by their knowledge of technology.
lines.cn: 年轻农夫怀着对农业的热爱，借助对技术的了解。

lines.t: To find inexpensive and appropriately sized tools, they collaborate and innovate.
lines.cn: 为了找到便宜且尺寸合适的工具，他们协作创新。

lines.t: Sometimes the old stuff just works better or more efficiently.
lines.cn: 有时，老东西就是更好用或更高效。

questions.stem: What do we learn from the passage about the food company Eat Grub?

options.A: It has turned certain insects into a new food source.
options.B: It has started to expand business outside the UK.
options.C: It has imported some exotic foods from overseas.
options.D: It has joined hands with Sainsbury's to sell pet insects.

questions.cn: 关于食品公司 Eat Grub，我们从文中了解到什么？

optionsCn.A: 它把某些昆虫变成了新的食物来源。
optionsCn.B: 它已开始向英国以外扩展业务。
optionsCn.C: 它从海外进口了一些异域食品。
optionsCn.D: 它与塞恩斯伯里联手销售宠物昆虫。

questions.stem: What does the speaker say about his first bite of roasted crickets?

options.A: It was really unforgettable.
options.B: It was a pleasant surprise.
options.C: It hurt his throat slightly.
options.D: It made him feel strange.

questions.cn: 关于他第一口吃烤蟋蟀，讲话者说了什么？

optionsCn.C: 它轻微弄伤了他的喉咙。
optionsCn.D: 它让他感觉很奇怪。

questions.stem: What does Eat Grub say about its dried crickets?

options.A: They are more tasty than beef, chicken or pork.
options.B: They are more nutritious than soups and salads.
options.C: They contain more protein than conventional meats.
options.D: They will soon gain popularity throughout the world.

questions.cn: Eat Grub 如何介绍它的蟋蟀干？

optionsCn.A: 它们比牛肉、鸡肉或猪肉更好吃。
optionsCn.B: 它们比汤和沙拉更有营养。
optionsCn.C: 它们比传统肉类含更多蛋白质。
optionsCn.D: 它们很快就会风靡全球。

questions.stem: What does the passage say about insect farming?

options.A: It is environmentally friendly.
options.B: It is a promising industry.
options.C: It requires new technology.
options.D: It saves huge amounts of labour.

questions.cn: 关于养殖昆虫，文章说了什么？

optionsCn.B: 它是一个有前景的产业。
optionsCn.D: 它节省大量劳动力。

lines.t: Passage 2.
lines.cn: 短文二。

lines.t: Eat Grub is Britain's first new food company that breaks Western food boundaries by introducing edible insects as a new source of food.
lines.cn: Eat Grub 是英国第一家突破西方饮食边界的食品新公司，它引入可食用昆虫作为新的食物来源。

lines.t: And Sainsbury's is the first UK supermarket to stock the company's crunchy roasted crickets.
lines.cn: 而塞恩斯伯里超市是英国第一家上架该公司香脆烤蟋蟀的超市。

lines.t: Sainsbury's insists that such food is no joke and could be a new sustainable source of protein.
lines.cn: 塞恩斯伯里坚持认为，这种食品不是玩笑，它可能成为一种新的可持续蛋白质来源。

lines.t: Out of curiosity, I paid a visit to Sainsbury's.
lines.cn: 出于好奇，我去了一趟塞恩斯伯里。

lines.t: As I put my hand into a packet of crickets with their tiny eyes and legs, the idea of one going in my mouth made me feel a little sick.
lines.cn: 当我把手伸进一袋长着小眼睛和小腿的蟋蟀时，想到要吃一只，我觉得有点恶心。

lines.t: But the first bite was a pleasant surprise.
lines.cn: 但第一口是个惊喜。

lines.t: A little dry and lacking in taste, but at least a wing didn't get stuck in my throat.
lines.cn: 有点干、没什么味道，但至少没有翅膀卡在我喉咙里。

lines.t: The roasted seasoning largely overpowered any other flavour, although there was a slightly bitter aftertaste.
lines.cn: 烤制的调味料在很大程度上盖过了其他味道，不过有一点点苦的余味。

lines.t: The texture was crunchy, but smelt a little of cat food.
lines.cn: 口感是脆的，但闻起来有点像猫粮。

lines.t: Eat Grub also recommends the crickets as a topping for noodles, soups and salads.
lines.cn: Eat Grub 还推荐把蟋蟀作为面条、汤和沙拉的配料。

lines.t: The company boasts that its dried crickets contain more protein than beef, chicken and pork, as well as minerals like iron and calcium.
lines.cn: 该公司自豪地宣称，其蟋蟀干所含的蛋白质高于牛肉、鸡肉和猪肉，还含有铁和钙等矿物质。

lines.t: Unlike the production of meat, bugs do not use up large amounts of land, water or feed, and insect farming also produces far fewer greenhouse gases.
lines.cn: 与肉类的生产不同，虫子不占用大量土地、水或饲料，而且养殖昆虫产生的温室气体也少得多。

lines.t: However, despite 2 billion people worldwide already supplementing their diet with insects, consumer disgust remains a large barrier in many western countries.
lines.cn: 然而，尽管全世界已有 20 亿人在饮食中补充昆虫，在许多西方国家，消费者的厌恶感仍是一大障碍。

lines.t: I'm not sure bugs will become a popular snack any time soon, but they're definitely food for thought.
lines.cn: 我不确定虫子是否很快就会成为流行零食，但它们确实值得深思。

questions.stem: Why do psychologists and educators study learning styles?

options.A: To categorize different types of learners.
options.B: To find out what students prefer to learn.
options.C: To understand the mechanism of the human brain.
options.D: To see if they are inherent traits affecting learning.

questions.cn: 心理学家和教育工作者为什么要研究学习风格？

optionsCn.A: 对不同类型的学习者进行分类。
optionsCn.D: 看它们是否是影响学习的固有特质。

questions.stem: What does the speaker say about one study mentioned in the 2008 review?

options.A: It was defective.
options.B: It was misguided.
options.C: It was original in design.
options.D: It was thought-provoking.

questions.cn: 关于 2008 年综述中提到的一项研究，讲话者说了什么？

optionsCn.D: 它发人深省。

questions.stem: What message does the speaker want to convey about learning at the end of the talk?

options.A: Auditory aids are as important as visual aids.
options.B: Visual aids are helpful to all types of learners.
options.C: Reading plain texts is more effective than viewing pictures.
options.D: Scientific concepts are hard to understand without visual aids.

questions.cn: 讲话者最后想传达关于学习的什么信息？

optionsCn.A: 听觉辅助与视觉辅助同样重要。
optionsCn.B: 视觉辅助对所有类型的学习者都有帮助。
optionsCn.C: 读纯文本比看图片更有效。
optionsCn.D: 没有视觉辅助，科学概念难以理解。

lines.t: Recording 1.
lines.cn: 录音一。

lines.t: Have you ever had someone try to explain something to you a dozen times with no luck?
lines.cn: 你有没有遇到过这种事：有人向你解释某件事解释了十几遍都没用？

lines.t: But then when you see a picture, the idea finally clicks.
lines.cn: 但你一看到图，就豁然开朗了。

lines.t: If that sounds familiar, maybe you might consider yourself a visual learner.
lines.cn: 如果这听起来很熟悉，也许你可以把自己当作视觉型学习者。

lines.t: Or if reading or listening does the trick, maybe you feel like you're a verbal learner.
lines.cn: 或者如果阅读或听讲对你有效，也许你觉得自己是言语型学习者。

lines.t: We call these labels learning styles.
lines.cn: 我们把这类标签称为学习风格。

lines.t: But is there really a way to categorize different types of students?
lines.cn: 但真的有一种方法可以对不同类型的学生进行分类吗？

lines.t: Well, it actually seems that multiple presentation formats, especially if one of them is visual, help most people learn.
lines.cn: 嗯，事实似乎是：多种呈现形式——尤其当其中一种是视觉形式——能帮助大多数人学习。

lines.t: When psychologists and educators test for learning styles,
lines.cn: 当心理学家和教育工作者检验学习风格时，

lines.t: they're trying to figure out whether these are inherent traits that affect how well students learn, instead of just a preference.
lines.cn: 他们想弄清楚：这些是影响学生学习效果的固有特质，还是仅仅是一种偏好。

lines.t: Usually, they start by giving a survey to figure out what style a student favours, like visual or verbal learning.
lines.cn: 通常，他们先给学生做问卷调查，弄清学生偏爱哪种风格，比如视觉学习或言语学习。

lines.t: Then, they try to teach the students something with a specific presentation style, like using visual aids,
lines.cn: 然后，他们尝试用特定的呈现方式——比如使用视觉辅助——教学生某些内容，

lines.t: and do a follow-up test to see how much they learned.
lines.cn: 再做后续测试，看他们学到了多少。

lines.t: That way, the researchers can see if the self-identified verbal learners really learned better when the information was just spoken aloud, for example.
lines.cn: 这样，研究者就能看出：例如，自我认定的言语型学习者，在信息只是被口头讲出时是否真的学得更好。

lines.t: But, according to a 2008 review, only one study that followed this design found that students actually learned best with their preferred style.
lines.cn: 但是，根据 2008 年的一篇综述，遵循这种设计的研究中只有一项发现：学生确实用自己偏好的风格学得最好。

lines.t: But the study had some big flaws.
lines.cn: 但那项研究有一些重大缺陷。

lines.t: The researchers excluded two-thirds of the original participants because they didn't seem to have any clear learning style from the survey at the beginning.
lines.cn: 研究者排除了三分之二的原始参与者，因为他们在最初问卷中似乎没有任何明确的学习风格。

lines.t: And they didn't even report the actual test scores in the final paper.
lines.cn: 而且他们甚至没有在最终论文里报告实际的测试分数。

lines.t: So, it doesn't really seem like learning styles are an inherent trait that we all have.
lines.cn: 所以，学习风格似乎并不是我们人人皆有的固有特质。

lines.t: But that doesn't mean that all students will do amazingly if they just spend all their time reading from a textbook.
lines.cn: 但这并不意味着所有学生只要把时间全花在啃教科书上就会表现惊人。

lines.t: Instead, most people seem to learn better if they're taught in several ways, especially if one is visual.
lines.cn: 相反，如果用多种方式教学——尤其当其中一种是视觉方式——大多数人似乎学得更好。

lines.t: In one study, researchers tested whether students remembered lists of words better if they heard them, saw them, or both.
lines.cn: 在一项研究中，研究者测试：学生是听单词、看单词、还是既听又看时，更能记住单词列表。

lines.t: And everyone seemed to do better if they got to see the words in print.
lines.cn: 而只要能看到印出来的单词，所有人都表现更好。

lines.t: Even the self-identified auditory learners. Their preference didn't seem to matter.
lines.cn: 甚至包括自我认定的听觉型学习者。他们的偏好似乎不起作用。

lines.t: Similar studies tested whether students learned basic physics and chemistry concepts better by reading plain text or viewing pictures, too.
lines.cn: 类似的研究还测试了学生通过阅读纯文本或看图片，是否更能学好基础物理和化学概念。

lines.t: And everyone did better with the help of pictures.
lines.cn: 结果，在图片的帮助下，所有人都学得更好。

tasks.title: Sec C · 第 2 组
tasks.context: Questions 19 to 21 are based on the recording you have just heard.

questions.stem: What do people often feel guilty about according to the speaker?

options.A: Not playing a role in a workplace revolution.
options.B: Not benefiting from free-market capitalism.
options.C: Not earning enough money to provide for the family.
options.D: Not spending enough time on family life and leisure.

questions.cn: 根据讲话者，人们常为什么感到内疚？

optionsCn.A: 没有在职场革命中发挥作用。
optionsCn.B: 没有从自由市场资本主义中获益。
optionsCn.D: 没有花足够时间在家庭生活和休闲上。

questions.stem: What did leading economists predict 90 years ago?

options.A: People would be working only fifteen hours a week now.
options.B: The balance of power in the workplace would change.
options.C: Technological advances would create many new jobs.
options.D: Most workers could afford to have a house of their own.

questions.cn: 90 年前顶尖经济学家预测了什么？

optionsCn.A: 人们现在每周只需工作 15 小时。
optionsCn.B: 职场的权力平衡会改变。
optionsCn.C: 技术进步会创造许多新工作。
optionsCn.D: 大多数工人能买得起自己的房子。

questions.stem: What is the result of denying workers' right to make their own choices?

options.A: Loss of workers' personal dignity.
options.B: Deprivation of workers' creativity.
options.C: Deterioration of workers' mental health.
options.D: Unequal distribution of working hours.

questions.cn: 剥夺劳动者自主选择权的结果是什么？

optionsCn.A: 劳动者个人尊严的丧失。
optionsCn.C: 劳动者心理健康的恶化。
optionsCn.D: 工作时间分配的不平等。

lines.t: Recording 2.
lines.cn: 录音二。

lines.t: Free market capitalism hasn't freed us. It has trapped us.
lines.cn: 自由市场资本主义并没有解放我们。它困住了我们。

lines.t: It's imperative for us to embrace a workplace revolution.
lines.cn: 当务之急是，我们必须拥抱一场职场革命。

lines.t: We are unlikely to spend our last moments regretting that we didn't spend enough of our lives slaving away at work.
lines.cn: 我们人生最后的时刻，不太可能后悔自己在工作上没辛苦卖命够多。

lines.t: We may instead find ourselves feeling guilty about the time we didn't spend watching our children grow, or with our loved ones, or traveling, or on the cultural or leisure pursuits that bring us happiness.
lines.cn: 我们更可能发现自己心怀愧疚：没能陪伴孩子成长的时间、没能与所爱之人共处的时光、没能去旅行，或没能投入那些带给我们幸福的文化与休闲活动。

lines.t: Unfortunately, the average full-time employee in the world works 42 hours a week, well over a third of the time we're awake.
lines.cn: 遗憾的是，全世界的全职雇员平均每周工作 42 小时，超过我们清醒时间的三分之一。

lines.t: Some of our all-too-precious time is being stolen.
lines.cn: 我们极其宝贵的时间正在被偷走。

lines.t: Office workers do around 2 billion hours of unpaid overtime each year.
lines.cn: 办公室职员每年无偿加班约 20 亿小时。

lines.t: So it's extremely welcome that some government coalitions have started looking into potentially cutting the working week to four days.
lines.cn: 因此，一些政府联盟已开始研究把每周工作时间缩短为四天的可能性，这实在令人欣慰。

lines.t: The champions of free market capitalism promised their way of life would bring us freedom, but it wasn't freedom at all.
lines.cn: 自由市场资本主义的鼓吹者曾许诺他们的生活方式会带来自由，但那根本不是自由。

lines.t: From the lack of secure affordable housing to growing job insecurity and rising personal debt, the individual is trapped.
lines.cn: 从缺少保障性可负担住房，到工作越来越没有保障、个人债务不断攀升，个人被困住了。

lines.t: Nine decades ago, leading economists predicted that technological advances and rising productivity would mean that we'd be working a 15-hour week by now.
lines.cn: 九十年前，顶尖经济学家预测：技术进步和生产率提升意味着我们现在每周只需工作 15 小时。

lines.t: That target has been somewhat missed.
lines.cn: 那个目标有些落空了。

lines.t: Here is the most malignant threat to our personal freedom, particularly as the balance of power in the workplace has been shifted so dramatically from worker to boss.
lines.cn: 这里是对我们个人自由最恶毒的威胁，尤其是职场权力平衡已从劳动者剧烈地滑向老板一方。

lines.t: A huge portion of our lives involves the surrender of our freedom and personal autonomy.
lines.cn: 我们生命中的很大一部分，是在交出自己的自由和个人自主权。

lines.t: It's time in which we are directed by the needs and desires of others and denied the right to make our own choices.
lines.cn: 在那段时间里，我们受制于他人的需要和欲望，被剥夺了做自主选择的权利。

lines.t: That's bad for us.
lines.cn: 这对我们有害。

lines.t: It's hardly surprising that over half a million workers suffer from work-related mental health conditions each year.
lines.cn: 每年有超过 50 万劳动者患上与工作相关的心理健康问题，这不足为奇。

lines.t: All told, 15.4 million working days were lost to work-related stress last year, a jump of nearly a quarter.
lines.cn: 总计而言，去年因工作压力损失了 1540 万个工作日，增长近四分之一。

lines.t: Yes, there are those who, far from being overworked, actually seek more hours.
lines.cn: 是的，有些人非但没有过度劳累，反而在寻求更多工时。

lines.t: But a shorter working week would enable us to redistribute hours from the overworked to the underworked.
lines.cn: 但更短的工作周，能让我们把工时从过劳者重新分配给开工不足者。

lines.t: We need to look at ways of cutting the working week without slashing living standards.
lines.cn: 我们需要想办法缩短工作周，而不削减生活水平。

lines.t: After all, the world's workers have already suffered the worst deduction in wages since the early 1800s.
lines.cn: 毕竟，全世界的劳动者已经遭受了 19 世纪初以来最严重的工资削减。

lines.t: And cutting the working week would be conducive to the individual, giving millions of workers more time to spend as they see fit.
lines.cn: 缩短工作周对个人有利，它给数百万劳动者更多时间，按自己的意愿支配。

tasks.title: Sec C · 第 3 组
tasks.context: Questions 22 to 25 are based on the recording you have just heard.

questions.stem: What does the speaker say about the dream airport in Berlin?

options.A: It is the worst managed airport in German history.
options.B: It is now the biggest and busiest airport in Europe.
options.C: It has become something of a joke among Germans.
options.D: It has become a typical symbol of German efficiency.

questions.cn: 关于柏林的梦想机场，讲话者说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 它是德国历史上管理最差的机场。
optionsCn.B: 它现在是欧洲最大最繁忙的机场。
optionsCn.C: 它已成为德国人之间的一个笑柄。
optionsCn.D: 它已成为德国效率的典型象征。

questions.stem: Why was there a need for a new airport in Berlin?

options.A: The city's airports are outdated.
options.B: The city had just been reunified.
options.C: The city wanted to boost its economy.
options.D: The city wanted to attract more tourists.

questions.cn: 为什么柏林需要一座新机场？

optionsCn.D: 该市想吸引更多游客。

questions.stem: Why did Berlin postpone the opening of its dream airport again and again?

options.A: The municipal government kept changing hands.
options.B: The construction firm breached the contract.
options.C: Shortage of funding delayed its construction.
options.D: Problems of different kinds kept popping up.

questions.cn: 柏林为什么一次次推迟梦想机场的启用？

optionsCn.D: 各类问题不断出现。

questions.stem: What happens while the airport remains unused?

options.A: Tourism industry in Berlin suffers.
options.B: All kinds of equipment gets rusted.
options.C: Huge maintenance costs accumulate.
options.D: Complaints by local residents increase.

questions.cn: 机场闲置期间发生了什么？

optionsCn.C: 巨额维护成本不断累积。
optionsCn.D: 当地居民的抱怨增多。

lines.t: Recording 3.
lines.cn: 录音三。

lines.t: Today I'm going to talk about Germany's dream airport in Berlin.
lines.cn: 今天我要谈的是柏林那座德国的梦想机场。

lines.t: The airport looks exactly like every other major modern airport in Europe, except for one big problem.
lines.cn: 这座机场看上去与欧洲其他每个大型现代机场一模一样，只除了一个大问题。

lines.t: More than seven years after it was originally supposed to open, it still stands empty.
lines.cn: 在原定启用时间过去七年多之后，它仍然空置着。

lines.t: Germany is known for its efficiency and refined engineering, but when it comes to its new ghost airport, this reputation could not be further from the truth.
lines.cn: 德国以高效和精湛的工程著称，但说到这座新的“幽灵机场”，这一名声与现实相去甚远。

lines.t: Plagued by long delays, perpetual mismanagement, and ever-soaring costs, the airport has become something of a joke among Germans, and a source of frustration for local politicians, business leaders, and residents alike.
lines.cn: 长期延期、管理不善、成本不断飙升——这座机场已成为德国人之间的笑柄，也让当地政界人士、企业领袖和居民都感到沮丧。

lines.t: Planning for the new airport began in 1989.
lines.cn: 新机场的规划始于 1989 年。

lines.t: At the time, it became clear that the newly reunified Berlin would need a modern airport with far greater capacity than its existing airports.
lines.cn: 当时情况已经很清楚：刚刚重新统一的柏林需要一座比现有机场容量大得多的现代机场。

lines.t: The city broke ground on the new airport in 2006.
lines.cn: 该市于 2006 年动工兴建新机场。

lines.t: The first major sign of problems came in summer 2010, when the Construction Corporation pushed the opening from October 2011 to June 2012.
lines.cn: 问题的第一个主要信号出现在 2010 年夏天，当时建设公司把启用时间从 2011 年 10 月推迟到 2012 年 6 月。

lines.t: In 2012, the city planned an opening ceremony, but less than a month beforehand, inspectors found significant problems with the fire safety system and pushed the opening back again to 2013.
lines.cn: 2012 年，该市计划举行启用典礼，但在不到一个月前，检查人员发现消防安全系统存在重大问题，启用时间再度推迟到 2013 年。

lines.t: It wasn't just the smoke system. Many other major problems subsequently emerged.
lines.cn: 不只是排烟系统。随后暴露出许多其他重大问题。

lines.t: More than 90 kilometres of cable were incorrectly installed.
lines.cn: 超过 90 公里的电缆被错误安装。

lines.t: Four thousand doors were wrongly numbered. Escalators were too short, and there was a shortage of check-in desks.
lines.cn: 4000 扇门编号错误。扶梯太短，值机柜台不够。

lines.t: So why, with so many problems discovered, didn't the Airport Corporation decide to give up on the project and start over?
lines.cn: 那么，发现了这么多问题，机场公司为什么不干脆放弃这个项目、从头再来？

lines.t: The reason is simple. People are often hesitant to terminate a project when they've already invested time or resources into it, even if it might make logical sense to do so.
lines.cn: 原因很简单：当人们已经在一个项目上投入了时间或资源后，即使从逻辑上讲放弃更合理，他们也常常不愿终止项目。

lines.t: The longer the delays continued, the more problems inspectors found.
lines.cn: 延期拖得越久，检查人员发现的问题就越多。

lines.t: Leadership of the Planning Corporation has changed hands nearly as many times as the opening date has been pushed back.
lines.cn: 规划公司的领导层更迭次数，几乎和启用日期推迟的次数一样多。

lines.t: Initially, rather than appointing a general contractor to run the project, the Corporation decided to manage it themselves, despite lack of experience with an undertaking of that scale.
lines.cn: 起初，该公司没有任命总承包商来管理项目，而是决定自己管理，尽管缺乏管理这种规模工程的经验。

lines.t: To compound the delays, the unused airport is resulting in massive costs.
lines.cn: 雪上加霜的是，闲置的机场正在产生巨额成本。

lines.t: Every month it remains unopened costs between 9 and 10 million euros.
lines.cn: 它每闲置一个月，就要花费 900 万至 1000 万欧元。

lines.t: Assuming all goes well, the airport should open in October 2020.
lines.cn: 假设一切顺利，机场应在 2020 年 10 月启用。

lines.t: But the still empty airport stands as the biggest embarrassment to Germany's reputation for efficiency and a continuing drain on city and state resources.
lines.cn: 但这座仍然空置的机场，是对德国高效名声的最大难堪，也持续消耗着市和州的资源。
